notes: Deviation (seed expansion left to DT1): §5.2 says the gap patterns are 'seeded and committed'. This file seals the seeds and the pattern parameters only; DT1 commits the seed-to-gap expansion code and the hash of its output before any T1g score is computed.
Deviation: whether patterns (a)-(c) apply to the short station, the control or both is not stated in §5.2; DT1 decides and records it.

a.applies_to: not stated in §5.2 (only (d) is restricted to the short station); DT1 decides
a.description: 20 random gaps of 3 h per month

b.applies_to: not stated in §5.2 (only (d) is restricted to the short station); DT1 decides
b.description: 5 random gaps of 12 h per month

c.applies_to: not stated in §5.2 (only (d) is restricted to the short station); DT1 decides

d.description: 10% of hours dropped at random, at the short station only

rule: datums spec §5.2 T1g gap injection: gap patterns (a)-(d) as written there; each pattern's seed is the first 8 bytes (unsigned big-endian) of SHA-256('otc-datums-t1g-v1|' + pattern letter), fixed in DT0b before any T1 data is reduced. How a seed is expanded into gap positions (RNG, month boundaries, overlap) is defined by the T1g harness (DT1) and is not part of this seal.
